name: Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Graph)
summary: Registering is fast, but enterprise tenants increasingly only let users consent to apps from verified publishers, and publisher verification needs a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account.
scenario: A multitenant agent that reads mail and calendar via Microsoft Graph for users in other companies' Microsoft 365 tenants.

composio.note: Check the Composio managed OAuth directory for the Outlook toolkit.

portal.accountNeeded: A Microsoft Entra work or school tenant. Personal Microsoft account registrations can't be publisher verified.

policyAndDomain.detail: A publisher domain must be set; for verification it must match your partner account's email domain or be DNS-verified in your tenant.

businessVerification.detail: Publisher verification requires a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (Partner One) account. Not strictly mandatory, but tenants using Microsoft's recommended consent policy block users from consenting to unverified apps.

adminApproval.detail: Tenants that restrict user consent, or permissions needing admin consent, require a tenant admin to grant consent.

appReview.detail: No Microsoft review of the app itself; each tenant's admins decide via consent settings.

paidOrPartner.detail: Partner program membership is free and verification has no charge, but the partner account must pass business verification.

securityAssessment.detail: Microsoft 365 App Certification is a separate, optional program.

time.note: Verification itself takes minutes if the partner account is already verified. The wait is for Partner Center business verification if you don't have it yet; Microsoft publishes no fixed time for that.

nextStep: Register a multitenant app in Microsoft Entra, add delegated Graph permissions and your redirect URI, and start Partner Center enrollment in parallel so publisher verification isn't the last-minute blocker.

prerequisites.text: An Entra work/school tenant with a DNS-verified custom domain (not *.onmicrosoft.com).
A Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that has completed verification, using the global account (PGA).
Someone who is both Application Administrator in Entra and Partner Admin in Partner Center, with MFA.

steps.title: Register a multitenant app
steps.detail: Entra admin center → App registrations → New registration. Choose accounts in any organizational directory (plus personal accounts if needed) and add your web redirect URI.

steps.title: Add delegated Graph permissions
steps.detail: Add only what the agent needs, e.g. Mail.Read, Mail.Send, Calendars.ReadWrite, offline_access. Avoid permissions that require admin consent unless your customers are admins.

steps.title: Create a client secret or certificate
steps.detail: Create a secret, note its expiry, and store it in your secret manager or Composio auth config.

steps.title: Set the publisher domain
steps.detail: Add and DNS-verify your company domain in the tenant and set it as the app's publisher domain.

steps.title: Get the partner account verified
steps.detail: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program and complete Partner Center verification with a business email on your domain.

steps.title: Mark the app publisher verified
steps.detail: In the app's Branding & properties, enter the Partner One ID and verify. The consent prompt then shows a blue verified badge.

steps.title: Write an admin consent guide
steps.detail: Give customers an admin consent link and instructions for the admin consent workflow for tenants that block user consent. An agent can draft this.

review.summary: No central app review. Adoption depends on each tenant's consent settings; verified publishers pass Microsoft's recommended policy.
triggers: A tenant restricts user consent to verified publishers or low-impact permissions
reviewersCheck: Tenant admins review the publisher name, verified badge, domain and requested permissions
review.meanwhile: Works immediately in your own tenant and in tenants that allow user consent for all apps (Microsoft's default).

blockers.issue: Users see 'unverified' or are told to ask an admin.
blockers.fix: Complete publisher verification, request fewer high-impact permissions, and give customers an admin consent link.

blockers.issue: Publisher verification fails: 'MPN ID does not exist' or domain mismatch.
blockers.fix: Use the partner global account ID, finish Partner Center verification first, and make the verification email domain match the publisher domain.
Since Nov 2020, with risk-based step-up consent enabled, users can't consent to new unverified multitenant apps requesting more than basic sign-in. Verify the publisher.

nuances.text: Microsoft's default lets users consent to any app for non-admin permissions, but Microsoft recommends restricting consent to verified publishers, and many enterprises do.
Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account, in B2C tenants or national clouds can't be publisher verified.

uncertainties: How long Partner Center business verification takes is not documented on the pages checked.
Graph permission names were not re-checked against the permissions reference in this pass.
Client secret maximum lifetime was not re-checked.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Configure how users consent to applications

corrections: Clarified that publisher verification is not universally required: Microsoft's default consent setting still allows unverified apps, but its recommended setting blocks them.
